description: Hello! We are Hurakán, a collective of future systems engineers proudly hailing from Huehuetenango, Guatemala. More than just classmates, we are enthusiasts passionate about the transformative power of technology and innovation. We firmly believe that code can save lives; therefore, our mission is to develop accessible and intelligent software that helps prevent risks and keeps the population informed in the face of any disaster.
summary: We have developed an advanced software capable of interpreting data from the NISAR satellite to address critical environmental and geological challenges. By detecting subtle changes imperceptible to the human eye, the system performs three primary functions: calculating ground subsidence in selected areas, tracking the melting process of specific glaciers, and monitoring the loss of flora in vital forest ecosystems such as the Amazon and El Petén.   This tool is essential for effective environmental management, climate change analysis, and risk mitigation. By delivering precise, early-stage data on land deformation, glacial retreat, and deforestation, the software empowers researchers and decision-makers to implement proactive conservation strategies and better protect vulnerable ecosystems worldwide.
details:
Our software extracts and processes multi-satellite orbital data to monitor critical environmental phenomena. Specifically, we utilize data from the Landsat satellite to analyze forest degradation, while relying on the NISAR satellite to calculate ground subsidence metrics and monitor glacial melting. Through an intuitive dashboard, users can select their specific area of interest by manually drawing custom coordinates on the map or by exploring pre-selected high-risk zones, such as the forests of El Petén or the glaciers of Greenland. Once an area is submitted for analysis, the system processes the satellite imagery and integrates the Gemini API to interpret the complex metrics, translating them into clear insights regarding potential environmental risks and affected locations.

The intended impact of this project is to democratize access to geospatial intelligence, allowing everyday citizens to easily check if their homes or local communities are near potential risk zones. To achieve this, we built the frontend graphical interface using Flutter and developed the backend processing engine with Python, sourcing our raw orbital datasets from NASA's Earthdata platform. Our solution stands out creatively by combining an interactive, user-friendly mapping interface, where users can freely draw regions and view historical year-by-year surface transformations, with generative AI. When designing the system, our team prioritized accessibility and ease of understanding, ensuring that complex multi-satellite measurements could be automatically analyzed and explained in plain language by Gemini for any user.
